title: How to say ‘no’: The power of defiance, with Sunita Sah, PhD

sentences.en: How often do you go along to get along, or say yes when you really want to say no?
sentences.zh: 你平时有多少次是为了迎合他人而选择妥协，或者在真正想说“不”的时候却说“好”呢？

sentences.en: We've all done it, agreed to a volunteer position that we didn't really have the time for, or held our tongue at the holiday dinner table to avoid a family fight,
sentences.zh: 我们都做过这样的事：答应承担一个其实根本没时间去做的志愿者岗位，或者在节日晚餐桌上守口如瓶以避免一场家庭争吵，

sentences.en: or kept quiet at work when speaking up could have helped a colleague avoid a mistake.
sentences.zh: 又或者在工作时保持沉默，而当时如果直言不讳本可以帮同事避免一个错误。

sentences.en: Today we're going to talk about the psychology of speaking up and saying no.
sentences.zh: 今天我们要探讨的是直言发声和说“不”的心理学。

sentences.en: Why is that so hard to do?
sentences.zh: 为什么这件事做起来这么难？

sentences.en: What does it mean to defy, to comply, or to consent?
sentences.zh: 反抗、顺从或同意究竟意味着什么？

sentences.en: And how can you strengthen your resolve and ability to say no when the situation calls for it?
sentences.zh: 当情势需要时，你又该如何增强自己说“不”的决心和能力？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association that examines the links between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学热议》（Speaking of Psychology），这是美国心理学协会（American Psychological Association）的旗舰播客，旨在探讨心理科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯（Kim Mills）。

sentences.en: My guest today is Dr. Sunita Sa.
sentences.zh: 我今天的嘉宾是苏妮塔·萨（Sunita Sah）博士。

sentences.en: Dr. Sa is an associate professor at Cornell University's
sentences.zh: 萨博士是康奈尔大学

sentences.en: S.C.
sentences.zh: 小约翰逊

sentences.en: Johnson School of Management, where she studies ethics, authority, compliance, and defiance,
sentences.zh: 管理学院的副教授，她在该校研究道德、权威、顺从与反抗，

sentences.en: including questions such as why we comply with bad advice, and how disclosure policies can backfire.
sentences.zh: 包括诸如我们为什么会听从糟糕的建议、以及披露政策如何适得其反等问题。

sentences.en: Her research has been published in many academic journals and covered by media outlets, including the New York Times, the Harvard Business Review, and Scientific American.
sentences.zh: 她的研究已发表在许多学术期刊上，并被《纽约时报》、《哈佛商业评论》和《科学美国人》等媒体报道。

sentences.en: Her new book is called Defy, The Power of No in a World That Demands Yes.
sentences.zh: 她的新书名为《反抗：在一个要求说“不”的世界里“不”的力量》（Defy, The Power of No in a World That Demands Yes）。

sentences.en: Dr. Sa, thank you for joining me today.
sentences.zh: 萨博士，非常感谢你今天能来参加节目。

sentences.en: It's wonderful to be here.
sentences.zh: 很高兴能来到这里。

sentences.en: Thank you, Kim.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，金。

sentences.en: The Oxford English Dictionary defines defiance as to challenge the power of another person boldly and openly.
sentences.zh: 《牛津英语词典》将反抗定义为大胆、公开地挑战另一个人的权力。

sentences.en: But in your book, you offer an alternative definition.
sentences.zh: 但你在书中提出了另一种定义。

sentences.en: Can you tell us what that is and why you felt defiance needed a new definition?
sentences.zh: 你能告诉我们那是什么吗？为什么你觉得反抗需要一个新的定义？

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 当然可以。

sentences.en: So, I've been fascinated by what that single word, defy, means for a very long time.
sentences.zh: 其实，很长一段时间以来，我一直对“反抗”这个单一词汇的含义着迷。

sentences.en: So, as a child, I was known for being an obedient daughter and a student.
sentences.zh: 我小时候是一个出了名的听话女儿和乖学生。

sentences.en: And I remember asking my dad at one point, what does my name mean?
sentences.zh: 我记得有一次我问爸爸，我的名字是什么意思？

sentences.en: And he told me, in Sanskrit, sunita means good.
sentences.zh: 他告诉我，在梵语中，苏妮塔的意思是“善良”。

sentences.en: And I mostly lived up to that.
sentences.zh: 我基本上一直不负这个名字。

sentences.en: So, I did what I was told.
sentences.zh: 所以我做着被告知要做的事。

sentences.en: I did my homework as expected, went to school on time.
sentences.zh: 按预期完成作业，按时上学。

sentences.en: I even had my hair cut the way my parents insisted.
sentences.zh: 我甚至按照父母坚持的要求剪了头发。

sentences.en: And these were the messages I received.
sentences.zh: 这些就是我接收到的信息。

sentences.en: You know, to be good, which means to be polite, to obey, to listen, not question authority.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，要做个好孩子，这意味着要有礼貌、要顺从、要听话、不要质疑权威。

sentences.en: And many of us get these messages from a young age.
sentences.zh: 我们很多人从小就接收到这些信息。

sentences.en: And we start equating compliance with being good and defiance with being bad.
sentences.zh: 我们开始把顺从等同于好，把反抗等同于坏。

sentences.en: But when I looked into it, and I've been studying this now for a very long time, I saw that there were some problems with that, in being so compliant.
sentences.zh: 但当我深入探究时——而且我研究这个已经很长时间了——我发现过分顺从其实存在一些问题。

sentences.en: So, for example, one survey found that nine out of ten healthcare workers, most of them nurses, did not feel comfortable speaking up when they saw a colleague making an error.
sentences.zh: 例如，一项调查发现，十分之九的医护人员（其中大多数是护士）在看到同事犯错时，觉得不敢直言不讳。

sentences.en: And it's the same across industries.
sentences.zh: 各行各业的情况都是如此。

sentences.en: So, in another survey of over 1,700 crew members of commercial airlines, about half of them felt uncomfortable saying something when they saw a mistake.
sentences.zh: 在对1700多名商业航空公司机组人员进行的另一项调查中，大约有一半人在看到错误时觉得不敢开口。

sentences.en: So, these could be life and death consequences.
sentences.zh: 所以，这些可能会带来生死攸关的后果。

sentences.en: We want these people to be speaking up when they see an error or a mistake.
sentences.zh: 我们希望这些人看到差错或错误时能够直言不讳。

sentences.en: And it made me start to wonder, is it sometimes bad to be so good?
sentences.zh: 这让我开始思考：太乖有时是不是一件坏事？

sentences.en: What do we sacrifice by being so compliant?
sentences.zh: 我们为了顺从而牺牲了什么？

sentences.en: And what I discovered now that I've been looking at this for years, even if it's not life and death situations, when we don't speak up, when we see something wrong, it can be quite
sentences.zh: 而我多年研究发现，即便不是生死攸关的情况，当我们看到不对劲却选择沉默时，这也会相当

sentences.en: draining and have an effect on us.
sentences.zh: 消耗我们的精力，并对我们产生影响。

sentences.en: And I often felt a lot of tension between that aspect of doing what was expected of me and doing what I thought that was right.
sentences.zh: 我经常在“做符合预期的事情”与“做我认为正确的事情”这两者之间感到巨大的内心拉扯。

sentences.en: And that inspired so much of my research.
sentences.zh: 这激发了我的许多研究。

sentences.en: And what I discovered that I think is crucial and really changed how I think is that we've misunderstood what it means to defy.
sentences.zh: 我发现了一件我认为至关重要且真正改变我思维方式的事情：我们误解了反抗的含义。

sentences.en: So, I'm not one to usually disagree with the Oxford English Dictionary.
sentences.zh: 我通常不是那种会反驳《牛津英语词典》的人。

sentences.en: After all, I grew up in the UK.
sentences.zh: 毕竟，我是在英国长大的。

sentences.en: But I think that definition of defiance that you described is too narrow and doesn't honor our agency.
sentences.zh: 但我认为你所描述的那个反抗定义太狭隘了，并没有尊重我们的自主性。

sentences.en: And so, my definition of defiance is that to defy means to act in accordance with your values when there is pressure to do otherwise.
sentences.zh: 因此，我对反抗的定义是：反抗意味着在面临压力而要求你做别的事时，依然按照自己的价值观行事。

sentences.en: So, it takes defiance and transforms it into a positive pro-social force for society.
sentences.zh: 所以，它将反抗转化为了对社会的一种积极、亲社会的正向力量。

sentences.en: Because if you think about it, Kim, all our individual acts of consent and dissent every day add up to the society that we live in.
sentences.zh: 因为如果你仔细想想，金，我们每天所有关于同意与不同意的个人行为，汇聚成了我们所生活的社会。

sentences.en: And so, it affects our lives, our workplaces, our communities.
sentences.zh: 因此，它影响着我们的生活、我们的职场、我们的社区。

sentences.en: And that's why I'm so passionate about it and think that we need to understand what defiance really means and the power behind it.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我对此充满热情，并认为我们需要理解反抗的真正含义及其背后的力量。

sentences.en: Now, as long as we're talking about language, let me ask you the difference between compliance and consent.
sentences.zh: 既然我们在谈论语言，请问你，顺从和同意有什么区别？

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: Well, the two are often conflated, but they are actually quite different.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这两者经常被混为一谈，但它们实际上截然不同。

sentences.en: So, to comply with something just means to go along with something.
sentences.zh: 对某事顺从，仅仅意味着随波逐流、顺应某事。

sentences.en: And it's usually externally driven.
sentences.zh: 这通常是由外部驱动的。

sentences.en: Somebody is asking you to do something or there's expectations in your organization or in society and it's to go along and do comply with that expectation.
sentences.zh: 有人要求你做什么，或者你的组织或社会中存在某种期望，而你去顺应并遵从那种期望。

sentences.en: Consent is not compliance.
sentences.zh: 同意不等同于顺从。

sentences.en: Consent is a thoroughly considered authorization that is an active expression of our deeply held values.
sentences.zh: 同意是一种经过深思熟虑的授权，是我们内心深处价值观的积极表达。

sentences.en: So, why do I say that?
sentences.zh: 那么，我为什么会这么说呢？

sentences.en: Well, I worked as a physician before I became an organizational psychologiSt.
sentences.zh: 在我成为一名组织心理学家之前，我曾做过医生。

sentences.en: And what I do in my research is take informed consent, the definition of informed consent from medicine and apply it to other decisions that we make in our lives.
sentences.zh: 我的研究工作就是将知情同意的概念——医学中知情同意的定义——应用到我们在生活中做出的其他决策中。

sentences.en: So, for informed consent, we need five elements.
sentences.zh: 因此，对于知情同意，我们需要五个要素。

sentences.en: And these are, so first of all, capacity.
sentences.zh: 它们是：首先，能力。

sentences.en: We need to have the mental capacity to make a decision.
sentences.zh: 我们需要具备做出决策的精神能力。

sentences.en: So, physicians assess patients for capacity.
sentences.zh: 所以，医生会评估患者的认知能力。

sentences.en: Is this patient too ill?
sentences.zh: 这位患者病得太重了吗？

sentences.en: Are they under the influence of any drugs or alcohol?
sentences.zh: 他们是否受到了任何药物或酒精的影响？

sentences.en: So, first of all, hopefully we have the capacity to make a decision.
sentences.zh: 首先，希望我们具备做出决策的能力。

sentences.en: And then next, we need knowledge.
sentences.zh: 接下来，我们需要知识。

sentences.en: So, we need information on the decision that we're about to make.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们需要关于即将做出的决策的信息。

sentences.en: But it's not just knowledge.
sentences.zh: 但不仅仅是知识。

sentences.en: It's not just receiving the information.
sentences.zh: 不只是接收信息。

sentences.en: It's understanding it, which is the third element.
sentences.zh: 而是理解信息，这是第三个要素。

sentences.en: What are the risks?
sentences.zh: 风险是什么？

sentences.en: What are the benefits?
sentences.zh: 收益是什么？

sentences.en: What are the alternatives?
sentences.zh: 替代方案有哪些？

sentences.en: And to really understand that.
sentences.zh: 并且要真正理解这些。

sentences.en: Then the fourth one is this freedom to say no.
sentences.zh: 第四个要素是说“不”的自由。

sentences.en: Because if we don't have the freedom to say no, it's not really consent.
sentences.zh: 因为如果我们没有说“不”的自由，这就不是真正的同意。

sentences.en: It's simply compliance.
sentences.zh: 这仅仅是顺从。

sentences.en: And if those four elements are there, then you can engage in the fifth element, which is your authorization.
sentences.zh: 如果这四个要素都具备了，你就可以进入第五个要素，也就是你的授权。

sentences.en: So, if you want to say yes with all those elements, you have the capacity, the knowledge, the understanding, the freedom to say no, then that's your informed consent.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果你在具备所有这些要素的情况下想要说“好”——你拥有能力、知识、理解力、说“不”的自由——那么这就是你的知情同意。

sentences.en: If you want to say no, that's your informed refusal.
sentences.zh: 如果你想说“不”，那就是你的知情拒绝。

sentences.en: Why do most people find it so hard to say no, even when we know we should, whether that's agreeing to an obligation we don't want or staying quiet when we see someone behaving
sentences.zh: 为什么大多数人发现说“不”如此艰难，哪怕我们明知应该这么做——无论是答应一个我们并不想承担的义务，还是在看到某人表现得

sentences.en: unethically?
sentences.zh: 不道德时保持沉默？

sentences.en: In those moments, what is it that holds us back from speaking up?
sentences.zh: 在那些时刻，究竟是什么阻碍了我们开口直言？

sentences.en: Well, we often actively resist defiance.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们经常会积极地抗拒反抗。

sentences.en: And there's a number of reasons I've found for this.
sentences.zh: 我发现原因有很多。

sentences.en: But one key reason is that we feel this enormous pressure to go along with other people, this social pressure.
sentences.zh: 但其中一个关键原因是，我们感到了顺从他人的巨大压力，也就是这种社会压力。

sentences.en: And I've seen this time and time again in my research, experiment after experiment.
sentences.zh: 我在自己的研究中一次又一次地看到了这一点，做了一场又一场实验。

sentences.en: So, let me describe the type of pressure that I'm talking about.
sentences.zh: 那么，让我来描述一下我所说的这种压力。

sentences.en: And it could range from small stakes situations to much larger ones.
sentences.zh: 它的范围可以从赌注很小的日常情境到影响重大的情境。

sentences.en: So, when I was working as a junior doctor, my first job, I received an invitation to meet with a financial advisor for free.
sentences.zh: 当年我作为初级医生工作、担任第一份工作时，我收到了一份与财务顾问免费会面的邀请。

sentences.en: And I remember that meeting really well because it was in the posh meeting room at work.
sentences.zh: 我把那次会面记得清清楚楚，因为它是在单位里豪华的会议室里进行的。

sentences.en: So, as posh as you can get on the National Health Service.
sentences.zh: 可以说是国民医疗服务体系（NHS）里能达到的最高档配置了。

sentences.en: It was a room I didn't even know existed.
sentences.zh: 那是个我甚至不知道它存在的房间。

sentences.en: It had a carpet.
sentences.zh: 里面铺了地毯。

sentences.en: There was a couch.
sentences.zh: 还有一张沙发。

sentences.en: I was like, how come I've never discovered this before?
sentences.zh: 我当时想，我以前怎么从来没发现过这个地方？

sentences.en: So, I went in after a long night on call.
sentences.zh: 所以，在经历了一个漫长的值班夜后，我走了进去。

sentences.en: And I sort of sank down on the sofa.
sentences.zh: 我有点陷进沙发里。

sentences.en: And Dan, who was the advisor when he walked in, he was tall, he was handsome, big smile, smart suit.
sentences.zh: 顾问丹（Dan）走进来时，他身材高大、英俊潇洒、笑容灿烂、穿着一身笔挺的西装。

sentences.en: And he greeted me warmly.
sentences.zh: 他热情地向我打招呼。

sentences.en: And he spent an hour talking with me.
sentences.zh: 他花了一个小时和我交谈。

sentences.en: He asked many questions, mostly about my finances.
sentences.zh: 他问了许多问题，主要关于我的财务状况。

sentences.en: He built up this amazing rapport.
sentences.zh: 他建立了这种极佳的融洽关系。

sentences.en: And after about an hour, he asked me whether he could write a report.
sentences.zh: 大约一个小时后，他问我是否可以写一份报告。

sentences.en: He would send it in a week.
sentences.zh: 他会在一周内发给我。

sentences.en: And he recommended that I invest in a couple of funds.
sentences.zh: 他建议我投资几只基金。

sentences.en: All of this was for free.
sentences.zh: 所有这些都是免费的。

sentences.en: So, I was impressed.
sentences.zh: 所以我印象深刻。

sentences.en: And I had to ask him, what's in it for you?
sentences.zh: 我不得不问他：“这对你有什么好处？”

sentences.en: And he said, well, there's no such thing as a free lunch.
sentences.zh: 他说：“天下没有免费的午餐。”

sentences.en: And he would receive a commission if I invested in the funds that he was recommending.
sentences.zh: 如果我投资了他推荐的那些基金，他会获得佣金。

sentences.en: So, he disclosed this conflict of intereSt.
sentences.zh: 因此，他披露了这个利益冲突。

sentences.en: And what was key for me is that that disclosure did change the dynamics of the situation.
sentences.zh: 对我而言关键在于，这种披露确实改变了局面的动态关系。

sentences.en: So, I did feel less trust in the advice, which is arguably the intended purpose of that disclosure.
sentences.zh: 因此，我对这个建议的信任度确实降低了，这可以说是该披露的意图所在。

sentences.en: But at the same time, I now felt more pressure to go along with his advice because I didn't want to signal that distrust to him.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，我现在感到了更大的压力要去顺从他的建议，因为我不想向他释放出不信任的信号。

sentences.en: I didn't want him to think that this disclosure had now corrupted the lovely rapport that had been built up.
sentences.zh: 我不想让他觉得这种利益披露破坏了好不容易建立起来的融洽关系。

sentences.en: And I started to feel really uncomfortable.
sentences.zh: 我开始感到非常不舒服。

sentences.en: And I just then just wanted to sign and say, okay, fine, I'll invest in these ones.
sentences.zh: 当时我只想签字说：“好吧，行，我投资这些就是了。”

sentences.en: And what's happening there is the psychological process of insinuation anxiety.
sentences.zh: 当时发生的是“言外暗示焦虑”（insinuation anxiety）的心理过程。

sentences.en: So, this is a distinct type of anxiety that arises when we worry about our non-compliance with another person's wishes.
sentences.zh: 这是一种独特的焦虑，当我们担心自己不顺从他人的意愿

sentences.en: It's going to be interpreted as a signal of distrust and insinuates that the person is not whom they appear to be or should be.
sentences.zh: 会被解读为不信任的信号，并暗示对方并非他们表面看起来那样、或者不应该是的那样时，这种焦虑就会产生。

sentences.en: That they're not trustworthy or competent or have integrity or benevolence.
sentences.zh: 暗示他们不值得信任、不称职、缺乏正直或善良。

sentences.en: And it's an aversive emotional state.
sentences.zh: 这是一种厌恶性的情绪状态。

sentences.en: We become so concerned with offending the other person, we comply with them.
sentences.zh: 我们变得过于担心冒犯对方，以至于顺从了他们。

sentences.en: Even in one-off situations I've found with strangers, we have a huge amount of compliance because we don't want to insinuate that our advisors, our co-workers,
sentences.zh: 我发现，即使在与陌生人的一锤子买卖中，我们也会有大量的顺从行为，因为我们不想暗示我们的顾问、我们的同事、

sentences.en: our friends are not trustworthy.
sentences.zh: 我们的朋友是不值得信任的。

sentences.en: So, I'm sure we can imagine a situation where a boss is asking you to do something.
sentences.zh: 所以，我确信我们可以想象这样一种情境：老板让你做一件事。

sentences.en: Everybody's going along with it, but you don't think it's right.
sentences.zh: 每个人都在随波逐流，但你觉得这不对。

sentences.en: But it's just too difficult to tell them that they're wrong, right?
sentences.zh: 但要告诉他们他们错了实在是太难了，对吧？

sentences.en: Or that we're at the hairdresser and we're sitting there and they're cutting away, cutting away.
sentences.zh: 或者我们在美发沙龙里，坐在那里看着他们咔嚓咔嚓地剪个不停。

sentences.en: And you're thinking, no, that's not what I wanted.
sentences.zh: 而你心里想的是：不，这不是我想要的。

sentences.en: And it's just really hard to sort of tell them, no, this is not good.
sentences.zh: 要对他们说“不，这不好”真的很难。

sentences.en: We normally just say, yes, thank you and tip and walk out and feel dreadful.
sentences.zh: 我们通常只会说：“好的，谢谢，给小费，走人”，然后感觉糟糕透顶。

sentences.en: And so, it happens in those everyday interactions.
sentences.zh: 所以，这种情况就发生在那些日常互动中。

sentences.en: But what my research has shown me is that it's also in larger stake situations.
sentences.zh: 但我的研究向我表明，它也发生在风险更高的情况中。

sentences.en: So, in medical scenarios, when your doctor discloses a conflict of interest, people feel more pressure, more insinuation anxiety to go along with it.
sentences.zh: 因此，在医疗场景中，当你的医生披露利益冲突时，人们会感到更大的压力、更多的言外暗示焦虑，从而选择顺从。

sentences.en: So, even though trust decreases, insinuation anxiety increases.
sentences.zh: 所以，尽管信任度下降了，但言外暗示焦虑却上升了。

sentences.en: And it depends on which force is greater as to whether they will take the advice or not and go along with that.
sentences.zh: 人们是否会接受建议并顺从，取决于哪种力量更强大。

sentences.en: So, it's really important to know what that feeling is, this insinuation anxiety, and name it.
sentences.zh: 因此，了解这种感觉——这种言外暗示焦虑——并说出它的名字非常重要。

sentences.en: Because once we name it, we know what we're dealing with and we can understand it.
sentences.zh: 因为一旦我们说出它的名字，我们就知道我们在面对什么，并且能够理解它。

sentences.en: So, what are some steps a person can take to overcome the pressure to comply?
sentences.zh: 那么，一个人可以采取哪些步骤来克服顺从的压力呢？

sentences.en: Are there things you can do in the short term, in the long term?
sentences.zh: 你有没有什么短期或长期可以做的事情？

sentences.en: And is this a kind of muscle you can train so it gets stronger?
sentences.zh: 这是一种可以通过训练变得更强的肌肉吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, I absolutely believe that.
sentences.zh: 对，我绝对这么认为。

sentences.en: So, in the short term, I'll tell you what happened to me when Dan asked me to invest in those funds,
sentences.zh: 所以，在短期内，我跟你讲讲当丹让我投资那些基金时发生在我身上的事：

sentences.en: is when things were starting to just get that little bit too uncomfortable and the silence was a little bit too much, I was thankfully saved by my beeper going off.
sentences.zh: 当时事情开始变得有点太让人不自在，空气安静得有点过头，幸运的是，我的寻呼机响了，把我解救了出来。

sentences.en: And that was not planned.
sentences.zh: 那可不是事先安排好的。

sentences.en: But I managed to leave the room and he was like, no worries, I'll send you everything as planned.
sentences.zh: 但我设法离开了房间，他说，没事，我会按计划把所有资料发给你。

sentences.en: But when he did, I had time to think about it and think about my extremely limited disposable income and think, well, actually, I don't want to invest in these particular funds.
sentences.zh: 但当他真的发过来时，我有时间去思考这件事，思考我极其有限的可支配收入，然后想，其实我并不想投资这些特定的基金。

sentences.en: And it was much easier for me to make that decision away from Dan.
sentences.zh: 而且，离开丹之后，我做那个决定要容易得多。

sentences.en: So, this is what I call the power of the pause.
sentences.zh: 所以，这就是我所说的“暂停的力量”。

sentences.en: If you can just pause rather than agreeing in the moment or on the spot, and especially if you can get some physical distance, that really helps decrease that signal of distruSt.
sentences.zh: 如果你能先暂停一下，而不是当场或立刻答应，尤其是如果你能拉开一些物理距离，那真的有助于降低那种不信任的信号。

sentences.en: Because if this is social pressure, what we want to do is reduce that sort of social interaction as much as we can.
sentences.zh: 因为如果这是社交压力，我们想要做的就是尽可能减少那种社交互动。

sentences.en: So, if we can make the decision in private, if we have an opportunity to change our mind, in all my experiments, I show that compliance goes down a huge amount.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果我们能私下做决定，如果我们有机会改变主意，我在所有的实验中都表明，顺从度会大幅下降。

sentences.en: But making the decision in front of the other person is what leads us to comply a lot of the time and shows us that our public behavior is not in alignment with our private preferences.
sentences.zh: 但在另一个人面前做决定往往会导致我们顺从，这也表明我们的公开行为与我们的私下意愿并不一致。

sentences.en: So, we really need to be aware of that.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们真的需要意识到这一点。

sentences.en: But what's even better than just sort of thinking about the power of the pause in the moment is to really train ourselves for defiance.
sentences.zh: 但比临时想起“暂停的力量”更好的，是真正训练自己去抗争。

sentences.en: Because if you're like me and you had a masterclass in compliance growing up, you don't actually have the neural pathways to know how to defy, and we need to train them.
sentences.zh: 因为如果你跟我一样，在成长过程中接受过顺从的“大师班”，你实际上并不具备如何抗争的神经通路，我们需要训练它们。

sentences.en: Because we know that training makes a big effect, right?
sentences.zh: 因为我们知道训练效果显著，对吧？

sentences.en: Our brains have what we call neuroplasticity.
sentences.zh: 我们的大脑具备所谓的神经可塑性。

sentences.en: So, the neural pathways can change.
sentences.zh: 所以，神经通路是可以改变的。

sentences.en: If we're wired to comply, we need to change that wiring.
sentences.zh: 如果我们天生倾向于顺从，我们就需要改变这种连线方式。

sentences.en: So, how can we do that?
sentences.zh: 那么，我们该怎么做呢？

sentences.en: Well, we can start anticipating situations that require defiance.
sentences.zh: 我们可以开始预判那些需要抗争的情境。

sentences.en: So, the next time I see a financial advisor, for example, I will know if they disclose a conflict of intereSt.
sentences.zh: 比如，下次我见到财务顾问时，我就会知道他们是否披露了利益冲突。

sentences.en: If anyone discloses a conflict of interest, I will have some familiarity with that.
sentences.zh: 如果有人披露了利益冲突，我会对此有所熟悉。

sentences.en: So, I find that surprise really disables defiance.
sentences.zh: 所以我发现，突发情况真的会让人失去抗争能力。

sentences.en: It makes us freeze.
sentences.zh: 它会让我们僵住。

sentences.en: But if we can anticipate something, we can then start visualizing it and role-playing or scripting it out and practicing it.
sentences.zh: 但如果我们能提前预判，就可以开始将其可视化、进行角色扮演、编写剧本并加以练习。

sentences.en: And it's that practice that changes the neural pathways.
sentences.zh: 正是这种练习改变了神经通路。

sentences.en: In terms of anticipating, I always get asked, how do we know, right?
sentences.zh: 说到预判，人们总是问我：我们怎么知道呢？

sentences.en: How do we know what we need to defy?
sentences.zh: 我们怎么知道自己需要抗争什么？

sentences.en: Well, a lot of situations in which defiance is called for are actually quite predictable.
sentences.zh: 其实，许多需要抗争的情境实际上是相当可预测的。

sentences.en: So, for example, I know in a particular faculty meeting, there will be one colleague that will always say something inappropriate.
sentences.zh: 比如，我知道在某个教职工会议上，总会有某个同事说出一些不得体的话。

sentences.en: You just know that this is going to happen.
sentences.zh: 你就是知道这会发生。

sentences.en: Perhaps you're in a job and you know, in this particular job, I might be asked to look the other way.
sentences.zh: 也许你正处于某项工作中，你知道在这个特定的工作中，我可能会被要求睁一只眼闭一只眼。

sentences.en: I might be asked to do something unethical.
sentences.zh: 我可能会被要求做一些不道德的事。

sentences.en: And you need to be prepared for that.
sentences.zh: 你需要为此做好准备。

sentences.en: So, that anticipation is really important.
sentences.zh: 所以，这种预判非常重要。

sentences.en: We can't anticipate everything, but we can anticipate a lot of things.
sentences.zh: 我们无法预判一切，但我们可以预判很多事情。

sentences.en: And we know the situations that we've struggled with in the paSt.
sentences.zh: 而且我们很清楚自己过去曾在哪些情境中苦苦挣扎。

sentences.en: And we can think about those and practice what we wish we had said.
sentences.zh: 我们可以思考那些情境，并练习我们当时希望说出口的话。

sentences.en: And why is that so important?
sentences.zh: 为什么这如此重要？

sentences.en: Well, there's this famous quote that's often attributed to Bruce Lee, but was actually a Greek poet, that I think really shows us the importance of practice and training.
sentences.zh: 有一个常被归功于李小龙但实际上出自一位希腊诗人的名言，我认为它真正向我们展示了练习和训练的重要性。

sentences.en: And that quote is, under duress, we don't rise to the level of our expectations.
sentences.zh: 那句话是：在压力之下，我们不会提升到期望的高度。

sentences.en: We fall to the level of our training.
sentences.zh: 我们会跌落到训练的水平。

sentences.en: And so, that's why it's so important to start practicing for defiance and learning the skill long before the moment of crisis.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么在危机来临很久之前，就开始为抗争进行练习并学习这项技能是如此重要。

sentences.en: I have to ask, though, why are we still here in light of such psychological studies as the Stanford Prison Experiment,
sentences.zh: 不过我不得不问，鉴于斯坦福监狱实验、斯坦福大学等心理学研究，为什么我们现在仍然……

sentences.en: Stanley Milgram's research, that we're still obeying authority?
sentences.zh: 斯坦利·米尔格拉姆的研究表明我们依然在服从权威？

sentences.en: That work is decades old, but we've still been to authority when we know we shouldn't.
sentences.zh: 那项工作已经过去几十年了，但当我们明知不该服从时，我们还是服从了权威。

sentences.en: So, do you think your book and your work is going to penetrate more deeply than that?
sentences.zh: 所以，你认为你的书和你的工作能比以前产生更深远的影响吗？

sentences.en: Well, I certainly hope so.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我当然希望如此。

sentences.en: I mean, that's the idea, right, is to make defiance accessible to everyone.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这就是理念所在，对吧？让每个人都能轻松进行抗争。

sentences.en: And Stanley Milgram's work was definitely an inspiration when I looked at the amount of obedience that we have.
sentences.zh: 当我看到我们表现出的顺从程度时，斯坦利·米尔格拉姆的工作确实给了我很多启发。

sentences.en: But what really fascinated me with that work was the defiant subjects.
sentences.zh: 但那项工作真正让我着迷的是那些抗争的实验对象。

sentences.en: What enabled them to defy?
sentences.zh: 是什么让他们能够抗争？

sentences.en: And that is what I do a really deep dive on.
sentences.zh: 这就是我进行深度研究的课题。

sentences.en: It's the kind of book I wish I had had growing up, a step-by-step strategy to learn the will and the skill to defy.
sentences.zh: 这是我希望自己成长时能读到的那种书，一本提供分步策略来学习抗争意愿与技能的书。

sentences.en: Exactly how can we do this and how can we practice this?
sentences.zh: 我们究竟该如何做到这一点，又该如何练习？

sentences.en: So, I want to make defiance accessible to everyone.
sentences.zh: 因此，我想让每个人都能轻松进行抗争。

sentences.en: Because with defiance, we often think that it is loud or aggressive or violent.
sentences.zh: 因为谈到抗争，我们通常认为它是喧闹的、具攻击性的或暴力的。

sentences.en: And it's none of those things.
sentences.zh: 然而它根本不是这些。

sentences.en: It's simply living in alignment with our values.
sentences.zh: 它仅仅是按照我们的价值观生活。

sentences.en: And it's accessible to everyone.
sentences.zh: 而且它是每个人都能做到的。

sentences.en: It's not a personality.
sentences.zh: 它不是一种个性。

sentences.en: It's a practice.
sentences.zh: 它是一种实践。

sentences.en: And that's a key point of misunderstanding what it means to defy is that we think we don't have the personality for it.
sentences.zh: 对抗争的误解的关键点在于，我们以为自己没有那种个性。

sentences.en: You don't need to have a large-than-life personality.
sentences.zh: 你不需要拥有光芒四射的宏大个性。

sentences.en: We can all defy in ways that are unique to us and with far less angst than we had in the paSt.
sentences.zh: 我们都可以用对我们而言独特的方式进行抗争，而且比过去少了很多焦虑。

sentences.en: So, it's just learning how to do that.
sentences.zh: 所以，这只是学习如何做到这一点的问题。

sentences.en: So, what are some good ways of saying no without offending another person or completely blowing up the situation?
sentences.zh: 那么，有哪些既不得罪别人又不会彻底激化矛盾的好方法来拒绝呢？

sentences.en: So, there's five stages of defiance that I've discovered.
sentences.zh: 我发现了抗争的五个阶段。

sentences.en: And the first one is tension.
sentences.zh: 第一个阶段是紧张。

sentences.en: And we can see that in the Milgram experiments, the obedience to authority experiments,
sentences.zh: 我们可以在米尔格拉姆实验、服从权威实验中看到这一点，

sentences.en: where the experimenter is asking a participant to give what they believe is harmful electric shocks to another person.
sentences.zh: 实验人员要求参与者向另一个人施加他们认为有害的电击。

sentences.en: You can see some of the subjects showing signs of tension.
sentences.zh: 你可以看到一些实验对象表现出紧张的迹象。

sentences.en: So, of nervous laughter, hesitating.
sentences.zh: 比如紧张地笑、犹豫不决。

sentences.en: And those moments are really important to acknowledge.
sentences.zh: 承认这些时刻非常重要。

sentences.en: Because often when we feel uncomfortable in a situation, we have a sign of tension that we know.
sentences.zh: 因为通常当我们在某种情境中感到不舒服时，我们会有一个自己熟知的紧张信号。

sentences.en: This is what always happens to me.
sentences.zh: 这总是发生在我身上。

sentences.en: Either you feel something in your stomach, you feel queasy, or your throat goes dry.
sentences.zh: 要么你胃里有什么感觉、感到恶心，要么你嗓子发干。

sentences.en: It's different for every person.
sentences.zh: 每个人都不一样。

sentences.en: It manifests in different ways.
sentences.zh: 它的表现形式各不相同。

sentences.en: But we have to get in touch with what is the tension that we have.
sentences.zh: 但我们必须弄清楚我们的紧张感究竟是什么。

sentences.en: Now, the second stage is really acknowledging that tension to ourselves.
sentences.zh: 现在，第二个阶段是对自己真正承认这种紧张感。

sentences.en: Because often we just disregard it.
sentences.zh: 因为我们通常会直接忽视它。

sentences.en: We think it's not worth our doubt.
sentences.zh: 我们觉得它不值得我们怀疑。

sentences.en: We think the other person knows better.
sentences.zh: 我们觉得对方懂得更多。

sentences.en: Or nobody else is saying anything.
sentences.zh: 或者没有别人在说些什么。

sentences.en: And it's going to be fine.
sentences.zh: 而且事情会没事的。

sentences.en: And so, we push it away.
sentences.zh: 于是我们把它推开。

sentences.en: And that's really a shame.
sentences.zh: 这真的很遗憾。

sentences.en: Because we're ignoring a really fundamental warning system that could be really powerful to us that we might need to defy.
sentences.zh: 因为我们忽视了一个非常基础的预警系统，它本可以对我们非常强大，而我们可能正需要它来抗争。

sentences.en: Now, coming to your question of how can we do this without offending the other person.
sentences.zh: 现在，回到你的问题：我们如何在不得罪对方的情况下做到这一点？

sentences.en: This is stage three of defiance.
sentences.zh: 这是抗争的第三阶段。

sentences.en: And it's actually a critical stage.
sentences.zh: 这实际上是一个关键阶段。

sentences.en: Because if we can get to stage three, the research shows you're more likely to get to the final stage five in the act of defiance.
sentences.zh: 因为如果我们能到达第三阶段，研究表明你更有可能在抗争行动中到达最后的第五阶段。

sentences.en: So, in this stage three, it's simply vocalizing your discomfort to someone else.
sentences.zh: 所以，在这个第三阶段，就是简单地向别人表达你的不适。

sentences.en: And it's just saying, I'm not comfortable with that.
sentences.zh: 也就是直接说：我对这个感到不舒服。

sentences.en: Or asking for clarification.
sentences.zh: 或者请求澄清。

sentences.en: What do you mean by that?
sentences.zh: 你这话是什么意思？

sentences.en: Have you considered this?
sentences.zh: 你考虑过这个吗？

sentences.en: And in this stage, you are still in a subservient position.
sentences.zh: 在这个阶段，你仍然处于顺从的地位。

sentences.en: You're just asking for clarification.
sentences.zh: 你只是在请求澄清。

sentences.en: Like, what is it that's really going on in this situation?
sentences.zh: 比如：这种情况下真正发生的事情到底是什么？

sentences.en: And so, I call it curiosity, not confrontation.
sentences.zh: 所以我称之为好奇，而不是对抗。

sentences.en: So, let's ask some questions and find out what's going on.
sentences.zh: 所以，让我们问一些问题，弄清楚到底发生了什么。

sentences.en: Because, again, a myth of defiance is that it's emotional and loud and aggressive.
sentences.zh: 因为同样地，关于抗争的一个神话是它充满情绪化、喧闹且富有攻击性。

sentences.en: And that's not what defiance is.
sentences.zh: 但抗争根本不是那样的。

sentences.en: It's simply acting in alignment with your values and knowing what's going on.
sentences.zh: 它仅仅是按照你的价值观行事，并了解正在发生的事情。

sentences.en: So, it's not about confrontation.
sentences.zh: 所以这无关对抗。

sentences.en: It's about living your life in alignment with integrity.
sentences.zh: 这关乎以正直的态度过好你的生活。

sentences.en: Do you think girls are still socialized to be more compliant than boys?
sentences.zh: 你认为女孩在社会化过程中仍然被塑造得比男孩更顺从吗？

sentences.en: In your research, are you seeing gender differences in how likely men and women are to be defiant?
sentences.zh: 在你的研究中，你是否看到男女在抗争倾向上的性别差异？

sentences.en: So, I've run quite a lot of studies on whether people will comply with bad advice.
sentences.zh: 我做过相当多的研究，关于人们是否会顺从糟糕的建议。

sentences.en: And in most of them, there were no gender differences.
sentences.zh: 在大多数研究中，没有发现性别差异。

sentences.en: Mulgram found the same in his studies, that the obedience to authority was the same for women as it was for men.
sentences.zh: 米尔格拉姆在他的研究中也发现了同样的结果，女性对权威的服从程度与男性相同。

sentences.en: So, in that aspect, I haven't seen gender differences.
sentences.zh: 所以在这方面，我没有看到性别差异。

sentences.en: It affects us all.
sentences.zh: 这影响着我们所有人。

sentences.en: This reluctance to defy affects us all.
sentences.zh: 这种抗拒抗争的心理影响着我们所有人。

sentences.en: There was one study, however, I did see a gender difference.
sentences.zh: 不过，确实有一项研究让我看到了性别差异。

sentences.en: And that is in what I call the ferry study, where we approached over 250 passengers going from Long Island to Connecticut.
sentences.zh: 那就是我所称的渡轮研究，我们在那里接触了从长岛开往康涅狄格州的250多名乘客。

sentences.en: And we had a middle-aged white man, sort of dressed quite smartly, approach passengers, as if he was an employee of the ferry, to ask them to fill out a short survey.
sentences.zh: 我们让一个穿着相当整洁的中年白人男子去接近乘客，假装他是渡轮的员工，请他们填写一份简短的调查问卷。

sentences.en: And the short survey was quite innocuous questions, such as, is the ferry clean?
sentences.zh: 这份简短的问卷包含一些非常无害的问题，比如：渡轮干净吗？

sentences.en: Was it leaving on time?
sentences.zh: 它准时出发吗？

sentences.en: It was very short.
sentences.zh: 非常简短。

sentences.en: And he promised them $5 if they finished the survey.
sentences.zh: 他承诺如果他们完成调查就给他们5美元。

sentences.en: So, after they finished the survey, he then asked them, well, I could give you the $5 as promised, or I could enter you into this mystery lottery that pays out between $0 and $10,
sentences.zh: 因此，在他们完成调查后，他接着问他们：我可以按承诺给你们5美元，或者我可以让你们参加一个神秘的彩票抽奖，奖金在0到10美元之间，

sentences.en: but the average payment is less than $5.
sentences.zh: 但平均奖金少于5美元。

sentences.en: So, once he said that, there was different conditions.
sentences.zh: 所以，当他这么说之后，有不同的条件。

sentences.en: With that alone and no advice about what to do, most of the people chose the $5 cash.
sentences.zh: 仅凭这一点，而且没有给出该怎么做的建议，大多数人选择了5美元的现金。

sentences.en: Just give me $5, right?
sentences.zh: 直接给我5美元，对吧？

sentences.en: Why would I enter a lottery where the expected value is less than $5?
sentences.zh: 我为什么要参加一个期望值低于5美元的彩票抽奖？

sentences.en: And so, it was 92% of people chose the cash, showing by far this is the preferred option.
sentences.zh: 结果有92%的人选择了现金，这清楚地表明这是首选方案。

sentences.en: In another condition, as well as presenting the two options, he also said, advise them to take the lottery.
sentences.zh: 在另一种情况下，除了提供这两种选择外，他还建议他们参加彩票抽奖。

sentences.en: Just recommended it.
sentences.zh: 只是推荐了它。

sentences.en: I think you should go for the lottery.
sentences.zh: 我认为你应该去抽奖。

sentences.en: Here, now, people took it.
sentences.zh: 这时，人们开始接受了。

sentences.en: 20% now took the lottery.
sentences.zh: 现在有20%的人接受了彩票抽奖。

sentences.en: Or just over.
sentences.zh: 或者略多一点。

sentences.en: And then when he disclosed an ulterior motive that he would also receive a bonus if they took the lottery, it more than doubled to 42%.
sentences.zh: 接着，当他透露了一个隐藏动机——如果他们参加彩票抽奖，他也会获得一笔奖金时，这个比例翻了一番多，达到了42%。

sentences.en: And when I asked the passengers afterwards why, it wasn't because they liked the advisor more.
sentences.zh: 当我事后问乘客为什么时，并不是因为他们更喜欢这位顾问了。

sentences.en: In fact, they liked him less once the disclosure was there.
sentences.zh: 事实上，一旦披露了动机，他们反而更不喜欢他了。

sentences.en: They felt much more uncomfortable to turn down the recommendation with disclosure than without, much like I did with Dan, the financial advisor.
sentences.zh: 比起没有披露动机的情况，披露动机后，他们会觉得拒绝推荐要尴尬得多，这很像我当年面对财务顾问丹时的感觉。

sentences.en: Here, we saw a gender difference.
sentences.zh: 在这里，我们看到了性别差异。

sentences.en: We weren't expecting one.
sentences.zh: 我们原本并没有预料到这一点。

sentences.en: But when we measured insinuation anxiety, it was far higher in the women than it was in the men.
sentences.zh: 但当我们测量暗示焦虑（insinuation anxiety）时，女性的焦虑程度远高于男性。

sentences.en: And that could be because it was a man giving the advice or the men didn't expect this man to be giving them
sentences.zh: 这可能是因为是一个男人在给出建议，或者男人们根本没指望这个男人会以任何方式向他们提供

sentences.en: benevolent advice in any way or they felt more comfortable to reject the advice.
sentences.zh: 善意的建议，或者他们觉得拒绝这个建议更自在。

sentences.en: But that experiment showed me there are situations where insinuation is more powerful for some people than it is for others.
sentences.zh: 但那个实验向我表明，在某些情况下，暗示对某些人比对其他人更有力量。

sentences.en: And we need to be aware of that.
sentences.zh: 我们需要意识到这一点。

sentences.en: What about cultural differences?
sentences.zh: 文化差异又如何呢？

sentences.en: In the U.S., we think of ourselves as a nation of individualists.
sentences.zh: 在美国，我们自认为是一个崇尚个人主义的国家。

sentences.en: And is that self-image correct?
sentences.zh: 这种自我认知正确吗？

sentences.en: Or are we just as likely to comply as people in other countries?
sentences.zh: 还是说，我们也和其他国家的人一样容易顺从？

sentences.en: I mean, the Milgram experiment was conducted 35 years after Milgram conducted it in the early 1960s.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，米尔格拉姆实验是在米尔格拉姆于20世纪60年代初进行该实验35年后再次开展的。

sentences.en: And what people found was that obedience hadn't changed over that time, even though there were actually increased perceptions of agency and autonomy.
sentences.zh: 人们发现，尽管当时人们对自主性和能动性的感知有所增强，但顺从度在这期间并没有改变。

sentences.en: So we do think of ourselves as possessing agency.
sentences.zh: 所以我们确实认为自己具备能动性。

sentences.en: And yet, with my experiments, I see an extremely high rate of compliance.
sentences.zh: 然而，在我的实验中，我看到了极高的顺从率。

sentences.en: So in some of the lottery experiments that I'm describing to you, I see rates of compliance of 85% or over.
sentences.zh: 因此，在我向你们描述的一些抽奖实验中，我看到顺从率达到了85%甚至更高。

sentences.en: And this is what researchers call a ceiling effect.
sentences.zh: 这就是研究人员所说的上限效应。

sentences.en: And that is very hard to get higher compliance.
sentences.zh: 而且要获得更高的顺从度非常困难。

sentences.en: So when I get asked, like, do you think we'll see different results in different countries?
sentences.zh: 所以当有人问我，比如，你认为我们在不同国家会看到不同的结果吗？

sentences.en: Well, if we're getting such high compliance in the U.S., then I'm not sure that we're going to sort of see higher compliance elsewhere.
sentences.zh: 嗯，既然我们在美国获得了如此高的顺从度，那我也不确定我们在其他地方是否会看到更高的顺从度。

sentences.en: And so I really do think we in America think that we are more defiant than we actually are and that we have possessed more agency than we actually display.
sentences.zh: 因此，我真的认为我们美国人觉得自己比实际表现得更叛逆，并且我们拥有的能动性也比实际展现出来的更多。

sentences.en: Now, sometimes it's dangerous to be defiant, whether that's for your career or health or mental health or for physical safety.
sentences.zh: 如今，有时表现叛逆是危险的，无论是对你的职业、健康、心理健康还是人身安全而言。

sentences.en: So how can people decide when is the right time to comply and when it's really necessary to defy?
sentences.zh: 那么，人们该如何判断什么时候是顺从的正确时机，什么时候又真的有必要进行反抗呢？

sentences.en: Great question.
sentences.zh: 问得好。

sentences.en: So defiance is never completely risk-free.
sentences.zh: 所以反抗从来都不是完全没有风险的。

sentences.en: And there are costs to defiance.
sentences.zh: 而且反抗是有代价的。

sentences.en: Like the things that we worry about that is going to cost me a relationship.
sentences.zh: 比如我们所担心的那些事，这可能会让我失去一段关系。

sentences.en: It might cost me a job.
sentences.zh: 它可能会让我丢掉工作。

sentences.en: It might be actually physically dangerous at points.
sentences.zh: 在某些时候，它甚至可能会带来人身危险。

sentences.en: But what we often forget is that there's costs to being compliant and giving up our agency.
sentences.zh: 但我们经常忘记的是，顺从和放弃能动性也是有代价的。

sentences.en: So bowing our head to others continuously and disregarding our values.
sentences.zh: 也就是不断地向他人低头，并无视我们的价值观。

sentences.en: So I recommend assessing the situation for defiance in two ways.
sentences.zh: 所以我建议从两个方面来评估是否应该反抗。

sentences.en: So two key questions that we want to ask.
sentences.zh: 也就是我们要问的两个关键问题。

sentences.en: And the first one is, is it safe?
sentences.zh: 第一个问题是，这安全吗？

sentences.en: So, of course, physically, but also maybe financially, psychologically, emotionally.
sentences.zh: 当然，不仅指身体安全，可能还包括财务、心理、情绪上的安全。

sentences.en: We want to ask ourselves those questions.
sentences.zh: 我们会问自己这些问题。

sentences.en: Again, we can never be completely safe.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，我们永远不可能做到绝对安全。

sentences.en: So the question is really, is it safe enough?
sentences.zh: 所以真正的问题是，够安全吗？

sentences.en: Is it safe enough?
sentences.zh: 够安全吗？

sentences.en: And then the second question is, is it effective?
sentences.zh: 第二个问题是，这有效吗？

sentences.en: Will it be effective?
sentences.zh: 这会有用吗？

sentences.en: Will I have some positive impact?
sentences.zh: 我会产生一些积极的影响吗？

sentences.en: And again, effective enough.
sentences.zh: 同样，也就是够有效吗？

sentences.en: Because some people don't really think about the positive impact because it's more important for them to take a stand for what they believe in,
sentences.zh: 因为有些人并不怎么考虑积极的影响，因为对他们来说，为自己信仰的事物挺身而出更为重要，

sentences.en: regardless of whether it has a positive impact or not.
sentences.zh: 无论它是否会产生积极的影响。

sentences.en: And so if we think about, like, some of the really famous acts of defiance in history, like Rosa Parks.
sentences.zh: 如果我们想一想历史上的那些著名反抗行为，比如罗莎·帕克斯。

sentences.en: I mean, she was not safe to defy.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，她进行反抗并不安全。

sentences.en: She was living under segregation, under mortal threat at times.
sentences.zh: 她生活在种族隔离制度下，有时面临着致命的威胁。

sentences.en: There was many consequences as well for her defiance that people don't talk about.
sentences.zh: 人们没有谈到的是，她的反抗也带来了许多后果。

sentences.en: It really had a huge impact on her.
sentences.zh: 这确实对她产生了巨大的影响。

sentences.en: She lost her job.
sentences.zh: 她失去了工作。

sentences.en: She was unemployed for 10 years.
sentences.zh: 她失业了10年。

sentences.en: There were many consequences.
sentences.zh: 有许多后果。

sentences.en: But when she was asked 10 years later, would she do it again?
sentences.zh: 但当10年后有人问她是否还会这样做时？

sentences.en: She was, of course, you know.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，她当然会。

sentences.en: And she had actually practiced for that moment.
sentences.zh: 而且她其实已经为那个时刻做了练习。

sentences.en: It wasn't a spontaneous decision like some people think.
sentences.zh: 这并不是像有些人认为的那样是一时冲动的决定。

sentences.en: She had been practicing that for that moment in years.
sentences.zh: 她为了那个时刻已经练习多年了。

sentences.en: And at that particular point, her defiance calculus, whether it was safe or effective enough, was a yes for her.
sentences.zh: 在那个特定的时刻，她对反抗的权衡——即是否足够安全或有效——对她来说答案是肯定的。

sentences.en: Now, here's a question for parents and other caregivers.
sentences.zh: 现在，这里有一个针对父母和其他照顾者的问题。

sentences.en: You don't want your toddler to be defiant every time you need to get them in their car seat.
sentences.zh: 你肯定不希望每当需要把幼儿放进汽车安全座椅时，他们都跟你作对。

sentences.en: So how do you teach children to respect adults and other children, but also to stand up to themselves when necessary?
sentences.zh: 那么，你如何教导孩子尊重成人和其他孩子，但在必要时也能坚持自己的立场呢？

sentences.en: Well, one of the things that I think we do for most children is train them in compliance.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为我们对大多数孩子所做的事情之一，就是训练他们的顺从性。

sentences.en: We train them in compliance a lot.
sentences.zh: 我们对他们进行了大量的顺从训练。

sentences.en: And if we misunderstand what defiance actually means, which is acting in alignment with your values, some of them, especially when it comes to teens,
sentences.zh: 如果我们误解了反抗的真正含义（即按你的价值观行事），那么其中一些人，尤其是当涉及到青少年时，

sentences.en: they're doing the exact opposite of what you tell them.
sentences.zh: 他们做的事情会跟你告诉他们的完全相反。

sentences.en: Now, I have a teenager right now, so some of these scenarios are very vivid in my mind, such as playing the Xbox, for example, and I would love him to do his homework instead.
sentences.zh: 现在，我刚好有一个青少年时期的孩子，所以其中一些情景在我的脑海中非常鲜活，比如玩Xbox，而我更希望他去做家庭作业。

sentences.en: And so I ask him, are you going to do your homework?
sentences.zh: 所以我问他，你打算做作业吗？

sentences.en: Well, and he's like, well, I was going to do my homework, but now that you've asked me to, I'm not going to do it.
sentences.zh: 然后他说，嗯，我本来打算做作业的，但既然你要求我做了，那我就不做啦。

sentences.en: And so what does that show us?
sentences.zh: 那么这向我们展示了什么？

sentences.en: Is that being defiant?
sentences.zh: 这算是在反抗吗？

sentences.en: Well, actually, in my definition, no, because what he's doing is listening intently to what I'm saying and acting in the exact opposite direction, which means that he's like,
sentences.zh: 嗯，事实上，按我的定义来看，不算，因为他所做的只是在仔细聆听我说的话，然后朝着完全相反的方向行事，这意味着他像是……

sentences.en: it's what I call false defiance.
sentences.zh: 这就是我所说的虚假反抗。

sentences.en: But defiance, like consent, comes from within.
sentences.zh: 但反抗就像同意一样，发自内心。

sentences.en: It's not from an external source.
sentences.zh: 它并非来自外部源头。

sentences.en: It doesn't depend on anybody else's expectations.
sentences.zh: 它不取决于任何其他人的期望。

sentences.en: It's coming from within you.
sentences.zh: 它是发自你内心的。

sentences.en: And so that's not really defiance.
sentences.zh: 所以这并不算是真正的反抗。

sentences.en: And what we need to do is actually train our children to be defiant.
sentences.zh: 我们需要做的是真正训练我们的孩子去学会反抗。

sentences.en: If we think of defiance as a good, positive force, we want to give them training in that.
sentences.zh: 如果我们把反抗视为一种美好的、积极的力量，我们就要在这方面对他们进行训练。

sentences.en: So one of the ways this really hit home was when I was about six or seven years old and I was walking home with my mom from the grocery store and my mom was wheeling the shopping cart,
sentences.zh: 真正让我深刻体会到这一点的一次经历是，大约在我六七岁的时候，我和妈妈从杂货店步行回家，我妈妈推着购物车，

sentences.en: which was just like an old rickety cart on two wheels, a bit like wheeled luggage that we take to the airports and it had our produce in it.
sentences.zh: 那只是一个带两个轮子的破旧旧推车，有点像我们带去机场的带轮行李箱，里面装着我们的农产品。

sentences.en: And it was quite a long walk back home.
sentences.zh: 走回家的路相当漫长。

sentences.en: I grew up in Yorkshire in England, and we wanted to take a shortcut through what we call there a snicket.
sentences.zh: 我在英国约克郡长大，我们想从当地人所说的一条“小巷”（snicket）走捷径。

sentences.en: A snicket is just a very narrow alleyway.
sentences.zh: 所谓的snicket只是一条非常狭窄的小巷。

sentences.en: And we decided to go through that alleyway on the way home to reduce the length of our walk.
sentences.zh: 我们决定在回家的路上穿过那条小巷，以缩短步行距离。

sentences.en: Now, in that alleyway,
sentences.zh: 然而，在那条小巷里，

sentences.en: we were confronted with about five or six teenage boys and they blocked our path and they shouted out some obnoxious things to us and told us to go back home.
sentences.zh: 我们遇到了大约五六个十几岁的男孩，他们挡住了我们的去路，对我们大喊大叫一些令人讨厌的话，并叫我们滚回家去。

sentences.en: Now, my mom is quite petite.
sentences.zh: 现在，我妈妈个子很小。

sentences.en: She's four foot ten at the moSt.
sentences.zh: 她身高最多只有四英尺十英寸（约147厘米）。

sentences.en: She was wearing her blue sari.
sentences.zh: 她穿着蓝色的纱丽。

sentences.en: She had her hair neatly plaited back, one single plait.
sentences.zh: 她的头发整齐地向后编成辫子，梳着单条辫子。

sentences.en: And the way I thought about my mom, if we think about compliance and defiance as binary, which I've realized it is not, you know, there's these stages of defiance.
sentences.zh: 在当时我对妈妈的看法中——如果我们把顺从和反抗视为二元对立，而我后来意识到并非如此，你知道的，反抗还有这些不同的阶段，

sentences.en: But if we do think about it that way, I had very neatly put her in the compliant box because she served everybody's needs.
sentences.zh: 但如果我们真的那样去想的话——我非常自然地把她归入了顺从的行列，因为她满足了所有人的需求。

sentences.en: She did the cooking, the cleaning, the grocery shopping.
sentences.zh: 她做饭、打扫卫生、买杂货。

sentences.en: She was always looking after other people.
sentences.zh: 她总是照顾别人。

sentences.en: She was not loud or aggressive.
sentences.zh: 她既不吵闹，也不具有攻击性。

sentences.en: And until that day, I thought she was completely compliant.
sentences.zh: 直到那一天之前，我都认为她完全是顺从的。

sentences.en: But when this happened and those boys stopped us, my reaction to them was instant.
sentences.zh: 但当这件事发生、那些男孩拦住我们时，我的第一反应非常本能。

sentences.en: So I grabbed my mom's arm and I averted my gaze.
sentences.zh: 我抓紧了我妈妈的手臂，移开了视线。

sentences.en: I did not want to look at them.
sentences.zh: 我不想看着他们。

sentences.en: And I just wanted to maneuver as fast as possible through them to go home.
sentences.zh: 我只想以最快的速度从他们中间穿过去回家。

sentences.en: And she didn't.
sentences.zh: 但她没有。

sentences.en: She stopped and she looked at them straight in the eye and she said, what do you mean?
sentences.zh: 她停了下来，直视着他们的眼睛说：“你们什么意思？”

sentences.en: And my heart started racing.
sentences.zh: 我的心开始狂跳。

sentences.en: I grabbed her arm even tighter and I whispered to her, no, come on, ma.
sentences.zh: 我把她的手臂抓得更紧了，对她低声道：“不，走吧，妈。”

sentences.en: And she shrugged me off.
sentences.zh: 而她把我甩开了。

sentences.en: She said no.
sentences.zh: 她说不。

sentences.en: And then she got the shopping cart.
sentences.zh: 然后她拿起了购物车。

sentences.en: She put it up upright and she put one hand on her hip.
sentences.zh: 她把它扶正，单手叉着腰。

sentences.en: And she looked back at the boys again and she said, what do you mean?
sentences.zh: 她又看着那些男孩说：“你们什么意思？”

sentences.en: And the boys didn't say anything.
sentences.zh: 男孩们什么也没说。

sentences.en: They were looking at each other.
sentences.zh: 他们面面相觑。

sentences.en: And she said, oh, yeah, you think you're so big and strong.
sentences.zh: 她说：“哦，是啊，你们觉得自己又大又壮。”

sentences.en: Big, tough boys, right?
sentences.zh: 了不起的硬汉，是吧？

sentences.en: Clever boys.
sentences.zh: 聪明的男孩。

sentences.en: And again, there was complete silence from their side.
sentences.zh: 对方依然是一片死寂。

sentences.en: And then one of the boys looked at the other and said, let's go.
sentences.zh: 然后其中一个男孩看了看另一个说：“我们走吧。”

sentences.en: And they just dispersed.
sentences.zh: 然后他们就散开了。

sentences.en: And I was astounded because I never expected that from my mom that day.
sentences.zh: 我大为震惊，因为我那天从没想过我妈妈会这样做。

sentences.en: And she grabbed the shopping cart and then she started walking back home really faSt.
sentences.zh: 接着她抓起购物车，迈开大步飞快地往家走去。

sentences.en: And I kind of stood frozen for a while before I ran after her.
sentences.zh: 我在原地呆立了一会儿，然后才朝她追了过去。

sentences.en: But what that really showed me was a couple of things.
sentences.zh: 但那件事真正向我展示了几点。

sentences.en: One is that defiance is not a personality.
sentences.zh: 第一点是，反抗并非一种性格。

sentences.en: It's a practice.
sentences.zh: 它是一种实践。

sentences.en: It's a skill set that we can choose to use or not.
sentences.zh: 它是一套我们可以选择使用或不使用的技能。

sentences.en: And it became clear to me that she had encountered those boys before.
sentences.zh: 我很清楚，她以前肯定也遇到过那些男孩。

sentences.en: But that day she did something different.
sentences.zh: 但那一天她做出了不同的举动。

sentences.en: She must have been practicing for it.
sentences.zh: 她当时一定为此练习过。

sentences.en: Or perhaps I was there in that moment and she wanted to show me something.
sentences.zh: 或者也许当时我在场，她想向我展示点什么。

sentences.en: And that day she did something different.
sentences.zh: 总之那一天她做出了不同的举动。

sentences.en: So even if we're being conditioned to comply the way I was, that I'm sure the way that my mother was as well, compliance might be our default, but it's not our destiny.
sentences.zh: 因此，即便我们像我曾经那样、也确信我母亲曾经那样被训练成顺从的人，顺从或许是我们的默认状态，但它绝不是我们的宿命。

sentences.en: The second thing that it showed me is that defiance might change you.
sentences.zh: 它向我展示的第二点是，反抗可能会改变你。

sentences.en: The instances where I've been able to defy, it is transformational.
sentences.zh: 在我能够进行反抗的那些时刻，它是具有变革意义的。

sentences.en: We feel more authentic, more honeSt.
sentences.zh: 我们会感到更加真实、更加坦诚。

sentences.en: It's more joyful life to be able to live in alignment with your values.
sentences.zh: 能够按照自己的价值观生活是一种更快乐的生活方式。

sentences.en: But it also changes the people that observe it.
sentences.zh: 但它也会改变目睹这一切的人。

sentences.en: I mean, my mom's defiance definitely had an impact on me.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我妈妈的反抗对我的影响绝对是深远的。

sentences.en: It stayed with me.
sentences.zh: 它一直留在我心中。

sentences.en: And it's what I call this ripple effect or the defiance domino effect is that it inspires other people to also go along with their values instead of going along with other people.
sentences.zh: 这就是我所说的涟漪效应或反抗多米诺骨牌效应，它激励着其他人也去坚守自己的价值观，而不是随波逐流去迎合他人。

sentences.en: And that's why it's really important.
sentences.zh: 这就是它真正重要的原因。

sentences.en: Because if we want to train our children to be defiant, these moments are what create society.
sentences.zh: 因为如果我们想训练我们的孩子去学会反抗，正是这些时刻在塑造着社会。

sentences.en: And what I really hope for with my book and making defiance accessible and changing our understanding is that one day, one of those teens would have spoken up and said, stop doing
sentences.zh: 我通过我的书真正期望的是，让反抗变得触手可及并改变我们的理解，从而有一天，这些青少年中的某个人会挺身而出，对他的朋友们说：别再对她

sentences.en: that to his friends.
sentences.zh: 做那种事了。

sentences.en: So my immigrant mother wouldn't have to.
sentences.zh: 这样我的移民母亲就不必亲自出面了。

sentences.en: So just to close, let me ask you, what are the big questions you still want to answer?
sentences.zh: 最后，我想问你，你还有哪些想要解答的重大问题？

sentences.en: What's next for you in research?
sentences.zh: 你在研究上的下一步计划是什么？

sentences.en: Well, I am researching what I call the voice empathy gap.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我正在研究我所说的“声音同理心鸿沟”。

sentences.en: So I've interviewed over 50 nurses and nurse managers.
sentences.zh: 我采访了50多位护士和护士长。

sentences.en: And what I've uncovered is that when you ask nurses why they don't speak up in a situation
sentences.zh: 我发现，当你问护士为什么在工作中看到一些错误时

sentences.en: at work when they see some errors, the reasons that they give are very different from why their nurse managers think that they don't speak up.
sentences.zh: 却选择保持沉默，她们给出的原因与她们的护士长认为她们不愿开口的原因截然不同。

sentences.en: So there is this gap in how it's viewed in that the nurses don't think it's safe or effective enough.
sentences.zh: 所以在如何看待这一问题上存在着鸿沟，护士们认为这样做不够安全或不够有效。

sentences.en: And the nurse managers think it's to do with the characteristics of the nurses, that they're
sentences.zh: 而护士长们则认为这与护士的性格特征有关，比如她们不愿为出错的事情承担责任，

sentences.en: not taking responsibility for things that go wrong or that they just don't have the ability or the skill set or the confidence to speak up.
sentences.zh: 或者认为她们只是缺乏发声的能力、技能组合或自信。

sentences.en: Looking into interventions to decrease that gap, because if we have a different understanding
sentences.zh: 我们正在探寻干预措施来缩小这一鸿沟，因为如果我们对导致人们保持沉默的原因存在不同的理解，

sentences.en: about what's causing people to speak up, then we have some kind of status quo where the environment and the culture doesn't change.
sentences.zh: 那么我们就会陷入一种环境和文化无法改变的现状之中。

sentences.en: And that's really important for us to manage if we want to create the right types of culture for people to speak up.
sentences.zh: 如果我们想为人们敢于发声创造正确的文化类型，管理好这一点至关重要。
